title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in South Korea: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in South Korea: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for South Korea: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in South Korea (the Republic of Korea) is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, completing key medical, legal, and financial steps while your family member retains full mental and legal capacity ensures their treatment choices and assets are protected under Korean law. Below, we set out the five official steps in order.

steps.title: Coordinate Hospice, Palliative Care, and National Health Insurance Coverage
steps.html:
• Statutory hospice and palliative care network: Under the Act on Decisions on Life-Sustaining Treatment for Patients in Hospice and Palliative Care or at the End of Life, patients diagnosed with eligible terminal conditions (including terminal cancer, AIDS, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chronic liver cirrhosis, and other conditions designated by the Ministry of Health and Welfare) can access inpatient hospice units, home-based hospice care (Gajeong Hoshpiseu), or consultative palliative care teams at designated hospitals [1][2].
  • Reduced co-payments under National Health Insurance: Ensure the attending specialist registers your family member under the Severe and Rare/Incurable Disease Copayment Reduction Program (Jungjeung Jilhwan Sanjeong Teukrye) with the National Health Insurance Service [3]. Once registered, statutory co-payments for covered inpatient and outpatient treatments related to the severe illness are reduced to 5% (or 10% for designated rare diseases), and hospice care is covered under National Health Insurance [2][3].
  • Long-Term Care Insurance (No-in Janggi Yoyang Boheom): If the illness causes significant physical functional decline (automatically eligible at age 65+, or under age 65 for designated geriatric/neurological conditions), apply to the National Health Insurance Service for a Long-Term Care Grade assessment to subsidise home-visit nursing, bathing services, assistive medical equipment, and care facility fees [3].

steps.title: Register an Advance Directive or Life-Sustaining Treatment Plan
steps.html:
• Advance Directive on Life-Sustaining Treatment (Sajeon Yeonmyeong Uiryo Uihyangseo): While your family member has full mental capacity, any adult aged 19 or older in South Korea can visit a designated registration agency - including branches of the National Health Insurance Service, public health centres, and major hospitals accredited by the National Agency for Management of Life-Sustaining Treatment - to receive mandatory one-on-one counselling and register an Advance Directive [1][3]. Once recorded in the national database of the National Agency for Management of Life-Sustaining Treatment, the directive is legally binding across all hospitals in South Korea [1].
  • Life-Sustaining Treatment Plan (Yeonmyeong Uiryo Gyehoekseo): For a patient already diagnosed as terminally ill or in the end-of-life process, the attending physician and a specialist in the relevant field can draft and register a physician-assisted Life-Sustaining Treatment Plan directly with the patient at the hospital [1]. This records the patient's legal decision to withhold or withdraw futile cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, hemodialysis, anti-cancer chemotherapy, or extracorporeal life support [1].
  • Designating a medical proxy via Guardianship Contract: Because South Korea's Life-Sustaining Treatment Act Otherwise relies on unanimous agreement of all immediate family members if no directive or plan was registered, your family member can reinforce their medical representation by naming a healthcare and personal-affairs guardian in a notarised Guardianship Contract (Im-ui Hugyeon Gyeyak) under the Civil Act [1][4].

steps.title: Execute Notarial Powers of Attorney, Guardianship Contracts, and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Voluntary Guardianship Contract (Im-ui Hugyeon Gyeyak): In South Korea, an ordinary Power of Attorney (Wiimjang) accompanied by a Certificate of Personal Seal Impression (Ingam Jeungmyeongseo, valid for 3 months from issuance) works for routine administrative errands, but banks often restrict large withdrawals once a customer loses mental capacity [4][6]. To create an enduring legal mandate that survives mental incapacity, your family member should execute a Voluntary Guardianship Contract (Im-ui Hugyeon Gyeyak) before a notary public and register it with the Family Court under the Supreme Court of Korea [4]. When capacity later declines, the Family Court appoints a Voluntary Guardianship Supervisor to activate the guardian's authority seamlessly [4].
  • Registering Electronic Signature and Seal Certificates: While your family member can still visit their local community service centre (Jumin Senteo) or log in via the Government24 Portal, verify their Personal Seal registration (Ingam) or Electronic Signature Certificate (Bon-in Seomyeong Sasil Hwak-inseo) [6].
  • Bank living trusts and direct account mandates: Major Korean commercial banks require in-person verification for high-value transfers. While your family member is mobile and has capacity, arrange in-branch pre-authorisations, set up automated hospital bill payments, or establish a Living Trust (Saengjeon Sintak / Will Substitute Trust) with their financial institution [4].

steps.title: Activate Disability Pension, Catastrophic Medical Aid, and Family Care Leave
steps.html:
• National Pension Service Disability Pension: If your family member is an active or former contributor to the national pension system whose illness has left persistent functional impairment after treatment, apply to the National Pension Service for a Disability Pension (Jang-ae Yeongeum, Grades 1 to 3) or a lump-sum disability compensation payment (Grade 4) [5].
  • Catastrophic Medical Expense Support (Jaenan-jeok Uiryobi Jiwon): For households facing high out-of-pocket medical bills (including certain non-covered treatments), apply through the National Health Insurance Service for the Catastrophic Medical Expense Support Program, which reimburses 50% to 80% of qualifying medical costs up to the statutory annual cap based on income brackets [2][3].
  • Statutory Family Care Leave (Gajok Dolbom Hyujik): Under the Equal Employment Opportunity and Work-Family Balance Assistance Act, employed family members in South Korea have a statutory right to take up to 90 days of unpaid Family Care Leave (Gajok Dolbom Hyujik) per year (usable in segments of at least 30 days), plus up to 10 days of short-term Family Care Leave (Gajok Dolbom Hyuga), and reduced working hours for family care to look after a seriously ill relative [2].

steps.title: Organize a Legally Valid Will, Beneficiary Records, and Cross-Border Documents
steps.html:
• Strict statutory formalities for wills under the Korean Civil Act: Korean courts strictly invalidate any will that deviates from the five statutory forms under Articles 1065-1070 of the Civil Act [4]. In practice, the two most reliable options are: (a) a Notarial Will (Gongjeung Yu-eon), prepared and recorded by a notary public in the presence of two witnesses while the testator has full capacity, which avoids post-death Family Court probate authentication (Geom-in); or (b) a Holographic Will (Japil Jeungseo Yu-eon), which must be handwritten in its entirety by the testator, stating the exact year, month, and day, the testator's full residential address, and full name, and stamped with the testator's personal seal (dojang) or thumbprint (computer-typed wills are void) [4].
  • Accounting for statutory forced heirship (Yuryubun) and tax planning: Under the Korean Civil Act, close heirs (spouse, children, and parents) hold a statutory minimum reserve share (Yuryubun - 50% of the statutory share for spouses and descendants, 33.3% for ascendants) [4]. Review major lifetime gifts and asset valuations against the Inheritance and Gift Tax thresholds administered by the National Tax Service [4].
  • Civil status certificates and Apostilles for overseas family: Obtain updated Family Relations Certificates (Gajok Gwangye Jeungmyeongseo) and Basic Certificates (Gibon Jeungmyeongseo) via the Supreme Court of Korea or the Government24 Portal, and secure Hague Apostilles for any cross-border powers of attorney or foreign property documents [4][6].

prefillQuestion: A family member is facing a serious or terminal illness in South Korea. We need an overview of the main official steps and contacts in South Korea for palliative care, powers of attorney, advance directives, and caregiver support.

contacts.name: National Agency for Management of Life-Sustaining Treatment
contacts.note: Official agency under the Korea National Institute for Bioethics Policy managing the national registry for Advance Directives on Life-Sustaining Treatment and Life-Sustaining Treatment Plans.

contacts.name: National Health Insurance Service
contacts.note: Administers the Severe Disease Copayment Reduction Program, hospice insurance coverage, Catastrophic Medical Expense Support, Long-Term Care Insurance, and Advance Directive registration.

contacts.name: Supreme Court of Korea
contacts.note: Oversees the Family Courts for Voluntary Guardianship Contract registration, probate matters, and the Electronic Family Registration System.

contacts.name: National Pension Service
contacts.note: Administers Disability Pension benefits and social security contribution records for contributors with severe illness or functional impairment.
